title: Enterprise Model Asset Registry, Supply-Chain Security & Multi-Node P2P Weight Distribution Selection

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Live `huggingface_hub` Internet Pulls on Pod Startup (`pickle .bin` Allowed)
tiers.architecture: Every Kubernetes GPU pod downloads weights directly from external HuggingFace Hub over NAT on startup without format or signature checks

tiers.tier: Tier 2: Baking 140 GB Model Weights Inside Monolithic Docker Container Images
tiers.architecture: Packaging PyTorch/CUDA runtime + 140 GB model weights into a single 155 GB Dockerfile layer pushed to container registry

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Private S3 / Blob Object Storage `initContainer` Sync (`aws s3 cp / azcopy` per Pod)
tiers.architecture: Decoupling weights to private S3/Blob storage, but all 32 pods pull 140 GB simultaneously from the same bucket endpoint

tiers.tier: Tier 4: `OCI Model Spec (ORAS)` Registry + `Safetensors + Sigstore Cosign` Gate + `Dragonfly / Spegel` P2P Distribution + Shared CSI Cache
tiers.architecture: Decoupled OCI Model Artifacts (`Harbor / ACR`) + Mandatory `safetensors` & `Cosign` Attestation + In-Cluster `Dragonfly` P2P Tree Distribution + Read-Only NVMe CSI Volume Mount

scenarios.scenario: Why Baking 140 GB Model Weights Inside a `Dockerfile` Breaks CI/CD and Kubelet Disks
scenarios.question: An engineering team packages a 70B BF16 model (`140 GB`) inside their vLLM Docker image; changing 1 line of Python wrapper code triggers a 155 GB image rebuild and push
scenarios.model_answer: Decouple **Engine Code Images (`12 GB`)** from **Model Weight Artifacts (`140 GB`)** using the **CNCF `ORAS / OCI Model Spec` (`Harbor / Azure Container Registry`)** and mount weights via a **CSI Volume Driver / Read-Only NVMe HostPath**: code updates push in 15 seconds without touching the 140 GB weight layers!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 rebuilds and re-pushes 155 GB layers on every code commit, filling up node `/var/lib/containerd` disks and taking 980s to roll out.

scenarios.scenario: Eliminating Registry Bandwidth Bottlenecks When 32 GPU Pods Scale Out Simultaneously (`Dragonfly / Spegel` P2P)
scenarios.question: During a morning traffic spike or canary rollout, 32 H100 nodes simultaneously pull a 140 GB model (`4.48 TB` total traffic), saturating the central registry/S3 gateway
scenarios.model_answer: Deploy **`Dragonfly` or `Spegel` In-Cluster P2P Chunk Distribution**: the registry/S3 sends the 140 GB model across the WAN/AZ boundary **only once (`140 GB` total egress)** while the 32 GPU nodes exchange 16 MB tensor chunks peer-to-peer over the 100G/400G intra-cluster network—completing all 32 nodes in **28 seconds**!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 (`1,420s`) and Tier 3 (`295s`) pull `32 x 140 GB = 4,480 GB` through the central gateway, leaving 32 expensive H100s sitting idle waiting for network I/O.

scenarios.scenario: Blocking Supply-Chain `Pickle (.bin / .pt)` Arbitrary Code Execution & Unsigned Weights
scenarios.question: A data scientist imports a community fine-tuned checkpoint from an external hub containing a malicious `pytorch_model.bin` (`pickle.loads` RCE payload)
scenarios.model_answer: Enforce an Airlock Quarantine Pipeline before any model enters the internal registry: (1) hard-block `pickle` formats (`.bin`, `.pt`, `.pkl`, `trust_remote_code=True`) and require zero-code **`safetensors` / `GGUF`**; (2) scan with `ModelScan / Fickling`; and (3) sign the approved OCI artifact with **`Sigstore Cosign`** verified by a Kubernetes `Kyverno / Gatekeeper` admission webhook (`0.0%` supply-chain RCE risk)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 downloads unverified weights directly from the internet into production GPU pods (`100.0%` exposure to pickle RCE and upstream repo tampering).

scenarios.scenario: Zero-Copy Memory-Mapped (`mmap`) Weight Sharing Across Co-Located Processes
scenarios.question: Multiple worker processes on the same 8-GPU node load the same model checkpoint from disk, duplicating host RAM usage and disk I/O
scenarios.model_answer: Mount verified `safetensors` shards from a local NVMe read-only cache volume with `mmap` Direct-I/O so page-cache / DMA buffers are shared once per physical node (`$21K/mo` TCO vs `$146K/mo` Tier 1, -85.6%)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 3 `initContainer` copies a separate 140 GB directory into every pod's ephemeral volume.

perturbation_checks.check: Upstream External Model Hub Outage or Rate-Limit (`HTTP 429` from Public Hub)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 28.0s Rollout | 0.0% Failure (100% Decoupled Internal OCI Registry + Local P2P Mesh)

perturbation_checks.check: Tampered Model Shard (`1 Flipped Bit` or Replaced Layer Tensor in Storage)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: Blocked at K8s Admission (`Cosign` SHA-256 Merkle Digest & SLSA Provenance Verification)

key_findings: Tier 4 (OCI Model Artifact Registry `Harbor/ACR` + `Safetensors/Cosign` Gate + `Dragonfly/Spegel` P2P Distribution + Shared NVMe CSI Cache) scales out a 140 GB model across 32 GPU nodes in 28.0 seconds (vs 1,420s live pull and 980s monolithic Docker image).
P2P tensor chunk distribution reduces cross-AZ/registry egress per 32-node rollout by 96.9% (from 4,480 GB to 140 GB) and cuts monthly storage/egress/idle-GPU TCO from $146K to $21K (-85.6%).
Enforcing `safetensors`-only ingestion + `ModelScan` + `Sigstore Cosign` admission control eliminates arbitrary code execution (`pickle` RCE) and upstream weight tampering (0.0% risk).
